# India applicability review packet

**Status:** COUNSEL_REVIEW_REQUIRED
**As at:** 2026-09-11T12:00:00+05:30
**Criterion:** BK-85-AC3
**Effect:** Counsel-ready analysis only. It is not a legal opinion, adoption record, or PASS.

## Scope and non-claims

Nyaymalaw is an India-only legal-work system for advocates and firms. This review packet covers account administration, matter intake and work, conflict screening, retrieval, drafting, export, support, security, billing, processors, backups and telemetry. It separates present law from notified future duties and product policy from legal compulsion.

Operating assumptions: The advocate or firm chooses why matter material is collected and how legal work is performed.<br>NM processes matter content only on documented customer instructions and separately determines purposes for its own account, billing and service-security operations.<br>India-region storage and no unapproved egress are stricter product policies, not a claim that the DPDP Act universally localises personal data.<br>Synthetic local work remains permitted; this packet does not authorise confidential pilot or production data.

Excluded without separate review: Any jurisdiction outside India or any practice-area promise not named in an approved coverage pack.<br>Sector-specific regulated workloads, including banking, insurance, securities, health and government data.<br>Children, biometric identification, voice biometrics, courtroom recording, sealed records and special-category matter protocols.<br>Cross-border processors, provider training on matter data, automated filing or sending, and direct client communication by NM.

Official sources:

- [IN-01 — Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023](https://www.meity.gov.in/static/uploads/2024/02/Digital-Personal-Data-Protection-Act-2023.pdf): Assented on 11 August 2023; individual provisions commence only on dates appointed under section 1(2), now specified by G.S.R. 843(E).
- [IN-02 — DPDP Act commencement notification](https://www.meity.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/11/c56ceae6c383460ca69577428d36828b.pdf): Sections 1(2), 2, 18-26, 35, 38-43 and 44(1),(3) commenced on publication; section 6(9) and 27(1)(d) commence on 13 November 2026; sections 3-5, 6(1)-(8),(10), 7-17, the remainder of 27, 28-34, 36, 37 and 44(2) commence on 13 May 2027.
- [IN-03 — Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025](https://www.meity.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/11/53450e6e5dc0bfa85ebd78686cadad39.pdf): Rules 1, 2 and 17-21 commenced on publication; rule 4 commences on 13 November 2026; rules 3, 5-16, 22 and 23 commence on 13 May 2027. The MeitY register also lists a 16 December 2025 corrigendum, which counsel must check against the operative text.
- [IN-04 — Information Technology Act, 2000](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/handle/123456789/15442): Current consolidated Act. Section 43A remains in the Act until DPDP Act section 44(2) commences on 13 May 2027; sections 70B and 72A remain separately material.
- [IN-05 — Information Technology (Reasonable Security Practices and Procedures and Sensitive Personal Data or Information) Rules, 2011](https://upload.indiacode.nic.in/showfile?actid=AC_CEN_45_76_00001_200021_1517807324077&filename=GSR313E_10511%281%29_0.pdf&type=rule): Published and operative from 11 April 2011; remains relevant with section 43A during the transition to DPDP section 44(2).
- [IN-06 — MeitY clarification on the SPDI Rules](https://www.meity.gov.in/writereaddata/files/PressNote_25811.pdf): Official clarification issued after the SPDI Rules; not a substitute for the Act, Rules or facts.
- [IN-07 — CERT-In directions under section 70B(6) of the IT Act](https://www.cert-in.org.in/Directions70B.jsp): The directions became effective sixty days after issue and remain a current incident-response input on the review date.
- [IN-08 — Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/20063/1/a2023-47.pdf): In force from 1 July 2024.
- [IN-09 — Advocates Act, 1961 and Bar Council of India Rules](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/handle/123456789/12656?sam_handle=123456789%2F2490): The Act and applicable professional rules are current; the exact BCI, State Bar and court rules applicable to the signing advocate and product use must be verified in the signed review.
- [IN-10 — Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021](https://www.meity.gov.in/documents/act-and-policies/information-technology-intermediary-guidelines-and-digital-media-ethics-code-rules-2021-it-rules-2021-IjM5QjMtQWa): Current rules published under the IT Act; the applicability of intermediary duties depends on NM's actual service and legal classification.

## Legal roles by purpose

| Purpose | Firm | NM | Provider | Accountability | Boundary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Account registration, authentication, session control and user support metadata | not applicable | data fiduciary | data processor | NM determines the account and security purposes; its approved infrastructure providers act only under recorded instructions. | A firm administrator's separate employment or access-management purposes must be documented rather than implied. |
| Matter intake, storage, retrieval, analysis, drafting and advice support | data fiduciary | data processor | data processor | The advocate or firm determines the legal-service purpose and remains responsible for instructions, privilege, accuracy and professional judgment; NM enforces the instructed processing boundary. | NM becomes a separate fiduciary for any independent reuse; independent reuse of matter content is prohibited by default. |
| Conflict screening and engagement acceptance | data fiduciary | data processor | data processor | The firm owns conflict rules and acceptance decisions; NM performs only the recorded check and preserves access separation. | Cross-firm pooling or provider reuse is a new purpose and is prohibited without separate review. |
| Customer support, diagnosis and service recovery | data fiduciary | conditional by operation | conditional by operation | NM is a fiduciary for support administration and a processor when support accesses matter content under a bounded customer instruction. | Support cannot become standing matter access; approval, purpose, duration and audited withdrawal are required. |
| Fraud prevention, abuse control, security monitoring and incident compliance | conditional by operation | data fiduciary | data processor | NM determines its service-security purpose and notification operations; the firm separately owns incidents in its practice and its client communications. | Security necessity is not permission for routine matter-content logging or unrelated analytics. |
| Subscription, invoice, tax and payment administration | not applicable | data fiduciary | conditional by operation | NM owns its billing purpose and must separately classify payment providers that determine their own statutory or fraud purposes. | Billing-record duties do not justify retaining the matter corpus. |
| Advocate-approved export, sharing, filing preparation and receipt capture | data fiduciary | data processor | conditional by operation | The advocate decides recipient, authority and final act; NM prepares and records within the approved mandate. | Recipients may have independent roles; NM does not send or file merely because it prepared a document. |
| Model training, product improvement, analytics and evaluation | conditional by operation | data fiduciary | conditional by operation | NM would determine this separate purpose and therefore bears the burden of a separate permission and review. | Matter content is excluded by default; provider retention or training is prohibited unless separately reviewed, consented where required and explicitly enabled for an exact population. |

| Record class | Current duty/floor | Ordinary rule | Hold rule | Erasure/restore | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Matter originals, derivatives, indexes, drafts and advice | SPDI Rule 5(4), where applicable, requires no longer than purpose or other law; privilege/confidentiality continues after service but does not impose indefinite storage.; no universal term identified; erase when purpose or permission ends unless retention is required by law | A counsel-approved schedule per matter class, posture and client terms; derivative lineage follows the source. | A scoped legal hold suspends only conflicting destruction, names authority, custodian, population, start, review and release. | Write tombstones across originals, derivatives and indexes; a restored backup must replay later tombstones before exposure. | OWNER-FIRM and OWNER-RETENTION |
| Identity, authentication, sessions, notices and account preferences | Retain only for current account/security purposes and separately identified statutory claims or records.; purpose specific no universal term; purpose_and_permission_review_before_2027-05-13 | Delete or irreversibly separate obsolete account data after closure and security windows, preserving only justified audit facts. | A claim, investigation or lawful order may hold the exact account records it identifies. | Revoked sessions remain revoked after restore; deleted identity data cannot silently reappear. | OWNER-NM-PURPOSE and OWNER-RETENTION |
| ICT and security logs | CERT-In directions require secure retention of ICT logs for 180 days within Indian jurisdiction for covered entities; collect content-free events wherever possible.; 180_days_in_India_for_ICT_logs; one_year_from_2027-05-13_where_rule_6_applies | Keep the applicable maximum of current floors and the approved security purpose, then delete on schedule. | An incident or lawful investigation may hold a bounded subset with chain of custody. | Log deletion and hold release apply to archives and restored copies; never retain routine privileged content to satisfy a log-duration rule. | OWNER-CERT-POC and OWNER-INCIDENT |

| Counsel qualification, authority and signed approval evidence | Retain a restricted authority artifact or trusted reference and original-byte digest sufficient to verify who could decide the exact scope.; decision lifecycle plus challenge window; minimise personal data and preserve accountability | Repository stores only the minimum identity, authority basis, restricted reference, digest, dates and decision scope. | Preserve challenged, superseded and revoked decision history; do not overwrite it with the replacement. | Redact or delete excess personal data without destroying the auditable decision identity required for accountability. | OWNER-PRIVACY-LEGAL and OWNER-RELEASE |

| Knowledge of a personal data breach after the relevant DPDP duties commence | without delay | future_from_2027-05-13 | Each affected Data Principal | The applicable Data Fiduciary with OWNER-PRIVACY-LEGAL | Provide the rule 7 content in concise and clear form through the registered account or communication method. | Future design requirement on the review date; it must not be described as the present DPDP notification clock. |
| Knowledge of a personal data breach after the relevant DPDP duties commence | without delay then detailed report within 72 hours | future_from_2027-05-13 | Data Protection Board of India | The applicable Data Fiduciary with OWNER-PRIVACY-LEGAL | Send the initial known description without delay and the detailed rule 7 report within 72 hours unless the Board permits a longer period. | The future 72-hour detailed report does not replace the immediate first notice or the current CERT-In six-hour assessment. |
| A processor, client, insurer or other contract defines a security/confidentiality notification event | earliest applicable contractual window | conditional now | Named contractual contact | OWNER-PROCESSOR or OWNER-FIRM with OWNER-INCIDENT | Run the contractual notice in parallel and preserve proof of timing and content. | A contract can be shorter or broader than statute but cannot waive a mandatory public-law duty. |
| The matter, entity, order or regulated sector creates another reporting or preservation duty | as directed by the specific instrument | conditional review required | Court, regulator, law-enforcement body, client or other named recipient | OWNER-COUNSEL and sector owner | Identify the instrument, trigger, time unit, recipient, authorised content and conflict with privilege before release. | No universal sector or court clock is asserted for NM's India-only service. |

Run all potentially applicable clocks in parallel from the earliest known trigger. Do not wait for perfect classification before escalation or an available-information notice.

## Accountability

| Role | Answerable for | Cannot delegate | Required before |
|---|---|---|---|
| Firm accountable partner or sole advocate | Matter purpose, client authority, conflicts, third-party data, privilege, legal holds, advice and external action. | Professional judgment, client duty and final legal approval cannot be transferred to NM or a model. | Any confidential matter is admitted. |
| NM product/data-purpose owner | Account, billing and independent service purposes; notices, minimisation, product defaults and purpose changes. | NM's own fiduciary purposes cannot be relabelled customer processing by contract prose. | Confidential pilot scope is approved. |
| India privacy/legal owner | Instrument register, permission mapping, rights, retention conflicts, breach classification and legal-change review. | A framework, vendor certificate or agent-generated answer cannot make the legal applicability decision. | BK-85-AC3 is signed and each live-data gate is considered. |
| Named CERT-In point of contact and backup | Current contact registration, six-hour assessment/reporting route, time source and secure log availability. | Provider notification does not prove NM's own applicable notice was made. | Confidential pilot and incident rehearsal. |
| Security incident commander and deputy | Detection time, containment, clock ledger, evidence custody, communications, recovery and post-incident review. | Incomplete facts are recorded and supplemented; they cannot be treated as a reason to let a clock expire. | Any real data or externally reachable deployment. |
| Retention and records owner | Schedules, holds, releases, lineage, erasure, tombstones, backup replay and deletion evidence. | A storage lifecycle setting does not decide legal holds or prove physical deletion across derivatives. | Persistent confidential storage. |
| Processor and egress owner | Inventory, contract, region, purpose, training/retention settings, subprocessor change, exit and incident route. | Vendor availability or a procurement approval cannot grant processing permission. | Any provider can receive protected data. |
| Qualified Indian counsel reviewer | Dated applicability judgment, professional-rule position, material reservations and expiry/reassessment triggers. | Only a stated and evidenced qualified reviewer can sign counsel_review evidence. | BK-85-AC3 can confer PASS or inform live-data approvals. |
| Named release owner | Exact release manifest, current evidence, reservations, approvals, rollback and the enabled scope. | A green plan, stale review or approval for another gate cannot release this scope. | Confidential pilot and production. |

## Mandatory reassessment triggers

- Before 13 November 2026 and before 13 May 2027, even if no other change occurs.
- Any new Gazette notification, corrigendum, rule, binding judgment, CERT-In direction or regulator/court requirement affecting a recorded proposition.
- Any new legal entity, jurisdiction, State Bar/court, practice area, professional role, language, data class or coverage pack.
- Any new or changed processor, subprocessor, model, region, cross-border route, retention/training setting, support path or security telemetry sink.
- Any change to purpose, permission, notice, terms, client authority, retention schedule, hold operation or external action capability.
- Any material incident, failed control, regulator/client challenge, professional complaint or evidence that a role classification is wrong.
- Any confidential-pilot or production approval expiry, revocation, supersession or relevant release/configuration change.
- At the qualified reviewer's earlier chosen valid_until date.

## Counsel sign-off boundary

Current state: **not_recorded**. The signed record belongs at `docs/backlog/evidence/BK-85-AC3-counsel_review.json`.

An Indian-qualified advocate or equivalent authorised Indian legal reviewer must verify the official instruments, the actual product/entities/contracts and every reservation. The reviewer must state the authority basis and reference a restricted evidence artifact with its original-byte SHA-256 digest.

The reviewer chooses valid_until. It must be finite and should be no later than the earliest material trigger or 13 November 2026; renewal requires a new dated review rather than editing history.

Resolve or expressly carry every material reservation; set result to PASS only if the rubric is satisfied for the counted population; record remaining reservations as an array; place the completed record at the target path and update BK-85-AC3 to reference it. A template is generated beside this packet but is deliberately invalid until completed and signed.

A typed name, role label, framework mapping, or this generated packet cannot confer PASS.
